DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Grade Your Own Signal

STS-MS6-L3-10001300-MSVPA-CMF-EUR-01 • MS Music Grade 6 • Evaluating Personal Work Using Criteria
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Real intelligence work is mostly listening to the same tape twice. Elena, Tomasz, and Ingrid have one reel recorded in a Vienna rehearsal hall, and a sealed file that tells them exactly what to listen for: tempo, dynamics, and timbre. The file never says whether the recording is good. It only hands them the three things to judge it by, which is how musicians have graded their own playing for two hundred years.
If you recorded yourself playing or singing, which would you check first: how fast it was, how loud it was, or what it sounded like?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Elena doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Elena is doing and why she is doing it. Speak in two complete sentences.
2
What is Tomasz holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Tomasz is holding and why he needs it. Speak in two complete sentences.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and why she is doing it. Speak in two complete sentences.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say what room this is and how you know. Speak in two complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the mission board.
Look at the picture. Say what is on the mission board and why it is on the wall. Speak in two complete sentences.
6
What is Ingrid wearing?
Look at the picture. Say what Ingrid is wearing and why it helps you find her in the picture. Speak in two complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: MU:Cr3.1.6a — Evaluate personal work using teacher provided criteria (elements of music, sound sources). ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
